name: Chicken Pulao
description: Fragrant Pakistani chicken pulao with bone-in chicken, basmati rice and aromatic yakhni-style stock, finished on low heat for separate, flavourful grains.
ingredients: 3 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
method: Combine the chicken, about half the onion, half the ginger-garlic paste, half the whole spices, salt and the stock water in a pot. Simmer gently until the chicken is nearly tender and the liquid is flavourful.
Remove the chicken carefully and strain the stock. Measure how much stock you have so the liquid added to the soaked rice can be controlled rather than guessed.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the remaining onion until evenly golden. Add the remaining ginger-garlic paste and whole spices, then return the chicken and fry briefly.
Lower the heat, add the whisked yogurt gradually with the green chillies and cook until the yogurt is incorporated and excess moisture reduces.
Drain the soaked basmati well and add it gently. Pour in the amount of hot chicken stock appropriate for your rice variety and taste the cooking liquid for salt before absorption begins.
Cook uncovered until most of the liquid is absorbed and steam holes appear across the rice. Cover tightly, reduce to very low heat and let the pulao finish gently without repeated stirring.
Turn off the heat and rest covered for about 10 minutes, then fluff from the sides with a light hand and serve.
tips: Do not automatically pour in all the stock; basmati varieties absorb different amounts of liquid.
Avoid excessive stirring after adding rice to keep the grains intact.
storage: Cool leftover chicken pulao promptly, refrigerate covered and reheat the portion being served until thoroughly hot.
image_alt: Chicken yakhni pulao with separate basmati rice, bone-in chicken, fried onion and fresh coriander
image_caption: Chicken yakhni pulao with separate basmati grains, bone-in chicken and aromatic fried onion.
technique: Pulao flavour is carried by the seasoned cooking liquid. Build a well-flavoured chicken and spice base first, then add rice with a measured amount of liquid and finish with controlled steam rather than repeatedly opening and stirring the pot.
doneness_cues: The stock should taste pleasantly seasoned before the rice goes in; weak stock usually produces weak pulao.
As the rice nears completion, visible free liquid should be almost gone without the bottom smelling scorched.
A finished grain should be tender through the centre and separate when lifted gently.
Resting the covered pot briefly should allow steam to settle so the rice fluffs more cleanly.
mistakes: Using a weak or under-seasoned yakhni and trying to repair the rice only after it has absorbed the liquid.
Adding too much water for the particular rice batch.
Stirring often after the grains soften, which releases starch and breaks basmati.
Keeping the flame high after most liquid has been absorbed.
substitutions: Bone-in chicken contributes more flavour to the stock, but boneless thigh can be used with a shorter cooking time.
Different basmati brands absorb liquid differently; keep notes on the rice you use instead of forcing one ratio onto every batch.
If the stock is already salty, reduce added salt before the rice goes in.
reheating: Break up chilled pulao gently, add a small splash of water, cover and reheat over low heat or in short microwave intervals until the chicken and rice are steaming hot.

faqs.question: Why does chicken pulao taste bland?
faqs.answer: Pulao depends heavily on the yakhni. Taste and correct the stock before adding rice because the grains absorb that seasoning.

faqs.question: Why did my pulao become mushy?
faqs.answer: Too much liquid, very long soaking, overcooking before dum, or vigorous stirring can all soften and break the grains.

faqs.question: Should pulao rice be soaked?
faqs.answer: A short soak can help many basmati varieties, but the ideal time depends on the rice. Follow the behaviour of your regular brand and drain it well.

serving: Serve hot with raita, green chutney or a simple onion-cucumber salad.
